# C-101 Ammonia Screw Compressor: Control Narrative (Draft A)

**Module:** C-101 (requirement prefix FR-C101). **Status:** Draft for process, operations and controls review. I have not seen the instrument index, cause-and-effect chart, alarm database or SRS, so this narrative writes out the interlocks and alarms in full (Sections 6 and 7). All numbers are in **Appendix A**. Values marked "confirm" are my provisional proposals, not owner data.

Test codes: **S** = simulate input at FAT and observe; **D** = demonstrate; **I** = inspect; **T** = timed test.

---

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

C-101 is a 400 hp screw compressor with slide valve capacity control. It starts through a soft starter (SS-101). No VFD is fitted. C-101 compresses ammonia vapor from the suction header and sends it downstream. The PLC controls start, stop, capacity, protection and the machine-room gas response for C-101.

| Interface | Direction | Content |
|---|---|---|
| Suction header, PT-101 | Upstream | Controlled variable |
| Discharge line, TT-103 | Downstream | Protection only |
| XV-120 (machine room main liquid solenoid) | Output | De-energize to close |
| EF-201 (emergency exhaust fan) | Output | High-speed command |
| Break-glass station (outside room) | Input | Hardwired |
| HMI (engine room office) | Bidirectional | Commands, status, alarms |
| Other compressors | Output | Common gas-shutdown signal |

**Out of scope:** other compressors, lead/lag sequencing, condenser and evaporator control, and oil-system auxiliaries (open items OI-02, OI-03).

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-001 | The PLC shall control C-101 only through the states in Section 3. | I |

---

## 3. States and transitions

### 3.1 States

| State | Meaning | Entry permissive | Exits |
|---|---|---|---|
| ST-0 TRIPPED | Latched trip. Run command off. | Any trip (Section 6) | T10 |
| ST-1 STOPPED-INHIBITED | Stopped. One or more start permissives false. | Power-up; T2; T5; T8; T10 | T1 |
| ST-2 READY | Stopped. All start permissives true. | T1 | T2, T3, T6 |
| ST-3 STARTING | Start sequence SQ-1 runs. | Operator start | T4, T5, T6 |
| ST-4 RUNNING | Motor runs. Capacity control active. | SQ-1 complete | T6, T7 |
| ST-5 STOPPING | Stop sequence SQ-2 runs. | Stop request | T8, T9 |

Load inhibit and forced unload are conditions inside ST-4, not separate states. The ISA-106 Hold function is met by load inhibit and by the stop request.

### 3.2 Start permissives (PERM-START)

All must be true:

1. No latched trip.
2. XS-130 healthy and gas shutdown cleared.
3. SS-101 ready, no fault.
4. ZT-105 at or below SP-10.
5. PT-101 above SP-20.
6. PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104 and ZT-105 not in bad-PV.
7. Start count in the rolling window (SP-31) is below SP-30.
8. Time since the last start is above SP-32.
9. HS-101 is in Auto.
10. Remote I/O healthy.

### 3.3 Transitions

| ID | From → To | Initiator | Condition | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | ST-1 → ST-2 | Auto | PERM-START true | Automatic |
| T2 | ST-2 → ST-1 | Auto | Any permissive lost | Automatic |
| T3 | ST-2 → ST-3 | Operator | Start command at HMI | Operator-initiated, then automatic |
| T4 | ST-3 → ST-4 | Auto | SQ-1 complete | Automatic |
| T5 | ST-3 → ST-1 | Auto | SQ-1 step 1 fails (before motor start) | Automatic |
| T6 | ST-2/3/4/5 → ST-0 | Auto | Any trip | Automatic |
| T7 | ST-4 → ST-5 | Operator or auto | Stop command, HS-101 to Off, or controlled-stop condition | Operator-initiated or automatic |
| T8 | ST-5 → ST-1 | Auto | Run feedback off | Automatic |
| T9 | ST-5 → ST-0 | Auto | Trip during stop | Automatic |
| T10 | ST-0 → ST-1 | Operator | Reset command and all trip causes clear | Manual |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-002 | The PLC shall allow T3 only in ST-2. | S |
| FR-C101-003 | The PLC shall allow T10 only when every trip cause is clear. | S |
| FR-C101-004 | After a PLC power-up, the PLC shall enter ST-1 (or ST-0 if a trip was latched before power loss). It shall not start C-101 automatically. | S: power cycle in ST-4 and ST-0 |
| FR-C101-005 | The PLC shall keep trip latches and the start-time history in retentive memory. | S |
| FR-C101-006 | The PLC shall count the start-time history against the real-time clock, including time with power off. | S |
| FR-C101-007 | The PLC shall count a start when the run command energizes. | S |

---

## 4. Regulatory control

### 4.1 Loop LC-101: suction pressure capacity control

| Item | Definition |
|---|---|
| PV | PT-101 |
| Setpoint | SP-01, limited to SP-02 to SP-03 |
| Output | Pulses on ZY-105L (load) and ZY-105U (unload) |
| Action | Load when PT-101 is above SP-01 plus deadband. Unload when PT-101 is below SP-01 minus deadband. |
| Modes | Auto, Manual |
| Active in | ST-4 only |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-008 | In Auto, the PLC shall pulse ZY-105L when PT-101 is above SP-01 plus SP-04. | S |
| FR-C101-009 | In Auto, the PLC shall pulse ZY-105U when PT-101 is below SP-01 minus SP-04. | S |
| FR-C101-010 | The PLC shall make the pulse width grow from SP-05 to SP-06 as the error grows to SP-07 beyond the deadband. | S |
| FR-C101-011 | The PLC shall wait at least SP-08 between pulses. | T |
| FR-C101-012 | The PLC shall never energize ZY-105L and ZY-105U together. | S |
| FR-C101-013 | The PLC shall block ZY-105L when ZT-105 is at maximum. It shall block ZY-105U when ZT-105 is at SP-09. | S |
| FR-C101-014 | In Manual, the PLC shall give one pulse of SP-05 width per operator load or unload command. | D |
| FR-C101-015 | A supervisor login shall be required to change SP-01. The PLC shall reject values outside SP-02 to SP-03. | D |
| FR-C101-016 | Mode change between Auto and Manual shall not cause a slide valve movement. | D |

### 4.2 Overrides (priority above Auto and Manual)

Priority, highest first: (1) forced unload, (2) load inhibit, (3) LC-101.

| ID | Condition | Effect | Reset | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-017 | II-104 at or above SP-22 | Block load pulses. Alarm IAH-104. | Auto, when II-104 is below SP-23 | S |
| FR-C101-018 | II-104 at or above SP-24 | Force unload pulses at SP-08 interval until II-104 is below SP-23. Alarm IAHH-104. | Auto | S |
| FR-C101-019 | TT-103 at or above SP-16 | Block load pulses. | Auto, when TT-103 is below SP-16 minus SP-25 | S |
| FR-C101-020 | PT-101 at or below SP-20 | Force unload pulses until PT-101 is above SP-20. | Auto | S |
| FR-C101-021 | Manual command during an override | Reject load commands. Accept unload commands. | n/a | D |
| FR-C101-022 | The current overrides (FR-017, FR-018) are masked in ST-3 until the up-to-speed signal is true. | | | S |

---

## 5. Sequences

### 5.1 SQ-1 Start (ST-3)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pulse ZY-105U. Hold until minimum. | ZT-105 at or below SP-10 | SP-11 | Stop pulses. Alarm XA-105. Go to ST-1 (T5). No motor start. |
| 2 | Energize SS-101 run command. Start the low-oil bypass timer (SP-14). | M-101 run feedback true | SP-33 | Remove run command. Trip TR-START. |
| 3 | Wait for soft starter up-to-speed. | SS-101 up-to-speed true | SP-34 | Trip TR-START. |
| 4 | Wait for bypass timer to end. Check PDT-102. | Timer done and PDT-102 above SP-13 | SP-14 plus SP-15 | Trip TR-OIL. |
| 5 | Hold slide valve at minimum. | Load release delay SP-35 done | SP-35 | None. Timer step. Trips stay active. |
| 6 | Release LC-101. Enter ST-4. | n/a | n/a | n/a |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-023 | The PLC shall run SQ-1 in the step order shown. | D |
| FR-C101-024 | The PLC shall run the bypass timer from the moment the run command energizes. | T |
| FR-C101-025 | The PLC shall treat a failure in step 2 to step 4 as a latched trip. | S |
| FR-C101-026 | The PLC shall not pulse ZY-105L during SQ-1. | S |
| FR-C101-027 | The PLC shall refuse the start if the permissive list is not true when the command arrives. | S |

### 5.2 SQ-2 Normal stop (ST-5)

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Pulse ZY-105U. | ZT-105 at or below SP-10 | SP-11 | Alarm XA-105. Continue to step 2. Start stays inhibited until ZT-105 is at or below SP-10. |
| 2 | Remove run command. | M-101 run feedback false | SP-36 | Alarm XA-106 (fail to stop). Stay in ST-5. Show prompt P-03. |
| 3 | Record stop time. Go to ST-1 (T8). | n/a | n/a | n/a |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-028 | The PLC shall unload the slide valve before it removes the run command in a normal stop. | D |
| FR-C101-029 | The PLC shall keep the stop alarm active until run feedback is false. | S |

### 5.3 Trip action (all trips)

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-030 | On any trip, the PLC shall remove the run command in the same scan. | S |
| FR-C101-031 | On any trip, the PLC shall latch the trip and record a first-out with time stamp. | S |
| FR-C101-032 | After a trip, the PLC shall pulse ZY-105U until ZT-105 is at or below SP-10 or SP-11 expires. | S |
| FR-C101-033 | The PLC shall reject a reset while any trip cause is active. | S |

---

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

No cause-and-effect chart was given, so the rows are written here. Trips below act through the PLC, except IL-04 and IL-05, which must also act through hardwired contacts (see SIS note).

| ID | Cause | Effect | Latched or auto-reset | Reset method | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| IL-01 | PDT-102 at or below SP-13 for SP-15, after SP-14 | Trip TR-OIL | Latched | Operator reset after cause clear | S |
| IL-02 | TT-103 at or above SP-17 for SP-18 | Trip TR-DISCH | Latched | Same | S |
| IL-03 | PT-101 at or below SP-19 for SP-21 | Trip TR-SUCT | Latched | Same | S |
| IL-04 | AE-110A or AE-110B at or above SP-27 | Trip C-101 (TR-GAS). Send shutdown to all compressors. De-energize XV-120. | Latched | Both detectors below SP-28, then operator reset. XV-120 reopens only on operator command. | S |
| IL-05 | XS-130 break-glass active | Same effect as IL-04 | Latched | Reset the station in the field, then operator reset | S |
| IL-06 | AE-110A or AE-110B at or above SP-26 | EF-201 high speed. Alarm AAH-110. | Auto | Both detectors below SP-28 for SP-29 | S |
| IL-07 | Starts in window at SP-30, or time since last start below SP-32 | Block start | Auto | Condition clears. HMI shows time to next start. | S |
| IL-08 | SS-101 fault input | Trip TR-STARTER | Latched | Clear fault at SS-101, then operator reset | S |
| IL-09 | Run feedback lost while commanded on | Trip TR-RUNFB | Latched | Operator reset | S |
| IL-10 | Remote I/O comms loss for SP-40 | Trip TR-COMMS | Latched | Operator reset after comms restore | S |
| IL-11 | Bad PV on PT-101, PDT-102 or TT-103 for SP-39 (running) | Trip TR-BADPV | Latched | Operator reset after PV restore | S |

**SIS note.** IL-04 and IL-05 are safety functions. The SRS (IEC 61511) owns their SIL, voting and hardwired logic. This narrative assumes the following; the SRS must confirm it (OI-01):

- Both functions open the M-101 run circuit and de-energize XV-120 through hardwired contacts that do not depend on the PLC.
- The PLC reads the same signals for state, first-out and alarm.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-034 to 044 | The PLC shall implement IL-01 to IL-11 as written. IDs FR-C101-034 (IL-01) to FR-C101-044 (IL-11) map one-to-one. | S per row |
| FR-C101-045 | The PLC shall use either detector (1oo2) for IL-04 and IL-06. | S |
| FR-C101-046 | The PLC shall keep XV-120 closed after a gas shutdown until an operator opens it from the HMI. | S |
| FR-C101-047 | The PLC shall not reset a gas shutdown or break-glass trip from a remote or automatic source. | S |

No alarm database was given. This list is the module need. Priorities are provisional, to be set in the ISA-18.2 rationalization.

| Alarm tag | Condition | Priority | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|
| PAL-101 | PT-101 at or below SP-20 | Medium | Check suction line and load. |
| PALL-101 | TR-SUCT | High | Find the cause. Reset. |
| PDAL-102 | PDT-102 at or below SP-12 (masked for SP-14 after start) | Medium | Check oil level and filter. |
| PDALL-102 | TR-OIL | High | Do not restart before inspection. |
| TAH-103 | TT-103 at or above SP-16 | Medium | Check load and cooling. |
| TAHH-103 | TR-DISCH | High | Same as TAH-103. Reset. |
| IAH-104 | Load inhibit by current | Low | None. Information only. |
| IAHH-104 | Forced unload by current | Medium | Check load and starter. |
| AAH-110 | Gas at or above SP-26 | High | Leave the room. Check for leaks. |
| AAHH-110 | Gas at or above SP-27 | High | Keep out. Call emergency contacts. |
| XA-130 | Break-glass active | High | Find the cause. Reset in the field. |
| XA-101 | Start blocked by IL-07 | Low | Wait. HMI shows the time. |
| XA-105 | Slide valve not at minimum | Medium | Inspect ZY-105U and ZT-105. |
| XA-106 | Fail to stop | High | Open the motor disconnect. |
| XA-107 | TR-START, TR-STARTER, TR-RUNFB | High | Inspect SS-101 and M-101. |
| XA-108 | Bad PV or detector fault, by tag | Medium | Repair the instrument. |
| XA-109 | HMI heartbeat lost | Medium | Check HMI network. |
| XA-110 | Remote I/O comms lost (TR-COMMS) | High | Check I/O network. |
| XA-111 | Power restored, C-101 stopped | Low | Do a field check. Then start. |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-048 | The PLC shall raise each alarm in the table at its condition. | S per row |
| FR-C101-049 | The PLC shall mask PDAL-102 for the SP-14 time after start. | T |

## 8. Abnormal handling

**Bad PV:** a PV is bad when the signal is below SP-37 or above SP-38, or when the module reports a fault.

| ID | Condition | Response | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-050 | PT-101 bad, running | Hold slide valve. Alarm. Trip TR-BADPV after SP-39. | S |
| FR-C101-051 | PDT-102 or TT-103 bad, running | Alarm. Trip TR-BADPV after SP-39. (The protective input is not available.) | S |
| FR-C101-052 | II-104 bad, running | Block load. Pulse unload to minimum. Alarm. Run continues. | S |
| FR-C101-053 | ZT-105 bad | Block load pulses. Allow unload pulses. Block start. | S |
| FR-C101-054 | One gas detector bad | Alarm. The other detector stays in service. | S |
| FR-C101-055 | Both gas detectors bad | Apply IL-06 (EF-201 high, alarm). | S |

**Communications**

| ID | Condition | Response | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-056 | HMI heartbeat lost for SP-41 | C-101 keeps its state, mode and setpoint. Alarm XA-109 is stored in the PLC. | S |
| FR-C101-057 | HMI start or reset command | The PLC shall accept the command only as a fresh, momentary edge. | S |
| FR-C101-058 | Remote I/O comms lost for SP-40 | IL-10. | S |

**Power loss and restart**

| ID | Condition | Response | Test |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-C101-059 | PLC power lost in ST-4 | The run command drops. XV-120 closes. | S |
| FR-C101-060 | Power restored | Per FR-C101-004. Alarm XA-111. | S |
| FR-C101-061 | Power restored with gas above SP-28 | Keep gas shutdown latched. | S |

**Fail positions** (confirm in the design review, OI-04)

| Device | Fail position |
|---|---|
| SS-101 run command | Off (de-energize to stop) |
| XV-120 | Closed (de-energize to close) |
| ZY-105L / ZY-105U | Both off (slide valve holds position) |
| EF-201 high-speed command | Runs at high speed on loss of PLC output (confirm) |

## Review notes

- **SP-20 versus SP-02:** I set the low-suction alarm (SP-20) below the lowest allowed setpoint (SP-02). This keeps alarms and forced unload from clashing with a valid setpoint. The trip level (SP-19) is below both.
- **Bad-PV trips on PDT-102, TT-103 and PT-101** are my fail-safe choice. Nuisance trips are the cost. Please confirm.
- **1oo2 gas voting** favors safety over availability. Confirm with the SRS.
- **STE pass:** I applied it to procedural text, prompts and requirement wording. The owner's operations team should check the prompt text for site vocabulary.
